s3.title: Behind the Bumpers | 103 Cybersonics | CRESCENDO FRC Robot

auto.text: The video description credits the team with a four-note auto; the interview does not describe it.

cycle.text: The under-bumper intake sweeps a note up into the pivoting shooter, which shoots from the subwoofer or from about the end of the stage.
The video description says the team shuttled notes through the whole Allentown event, which it won.

changed.text: About nine shooter iterations: side shooters lacked range, then top-and-bottom shooters flipped notes in the air, so the team added spin for a flatter, longer shot. Notes jammed in the transfer until orange straps went in. At Allentown, spacers in the pneumatics raised the shooter to recover its home-field shot.

outcome.text: 40-20-2 in official play; ranked 12 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 54.85, Daly).

solves.text: Leave room for the note to pass under the bumpers to the intake

facts.text: Yokes, main plate and top plate are made on a Tormach
Yokes were made a little bigger so that the note fits under the bumpers more easily

solves.text: Move a note from the floor to the shooter without it sticking in the transfer

facts.text: The top intake roller sweeps the note under into a bottom roller, then up into two more rollers
Sushi rollers on one roller sped the note up by a surprising amount, the team says
Orange straps sit where notes used to jam; dead rollers were tried first

functions.name: Shooter

solves.text: Stop notes flipping in the air and gain range

functions.type: pivoting shooter that spins the note

facts.text: Pivots up and down: the close shot is at the subwoofer and the long shot reaches about the end of the stage
Spin is meant to keep the note flat for longer shots
Small spacers in the pneumatics raised the shooter slightly at Allentown

solves.text: Keep a note from bouncing out of the amp

facts.text: The bar goes against the amp; with the shooter up, the note is fired in, and the bar blocks the bounce so that the note drops
Two pneumatic cylinders, each acting in one direction, flip the bar forward and back
The idea came from another team's robot and was tuned for rotation and arm length
The amp bar can rise only when a note is detected in the chamber, and it flips back by itself once the note leaves
Lights are meant to turn on when a note is detected
Bumper guards welded by team members

decisions.because: students learn to design a drive, and larger yokes let the note pass under the bumpers more easily
notes flipped in the air and the team wanted flatter, longer shots
decisions.instead_of: two side shooters, which lacked distance, and then top and bottom shooters

decisions.because: notes stuck and jammed at that point
decisions.instead_of: dead rollers, among other things tried
